source.title: Proclamation of Toussaint Louverture, Camp Turel

source: Frères et amis, je suis Toussaint Louverture ; mon nom s'est peut-être fait connaître jusqu'à vous. J'ai entrepris la vengeance de ma race. Je veux que la liberté et l'égalité règnent à Saint-Domingue. Je travaille à les faire exister. Unissez-vous à nous, frères, et combattez avec nous pour la même cause.
Il ne peut exister d'esclaves sur ce territoire, la servitude y est à jamais abolie. Tous les hommes y naissent, vivent et meurent libres et français.

source.title: Project notes: Toussaint Louverture, outline of his career

source: Toussaint, known before the Revolution as Toussaint Bréda after the Bréda plantation where he was enslaved, was freed in the 1770s. After the uprising of 1791 he became a leader of the insurgent forces and first fought alongside Spain against the French Republic. In 1794, after France abolished slavery, he joined the French Republic and fought against the Spanish and British. By 1801 he governed all of Hispaniola and issued a constitution that named him governor for life while keeping the colony part of France. Napoleon sent an expedition under General Leclerc in 1802. Toussaint was arrested in June 1802, deported to France, and died in prison at Fort de Joux in April 1803. He did not declare independence; Jean-Jacques Dessalines proclaimed it on 1 January 1804.
